findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: UDP-tunnel GSO super-packets (SKB_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL / SKB_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL_CSUM from vxlan/geneve/fou) are dispatched to __skb_udp_tunnel_segment() via skb_udp_tunnel_segment (called from udp4_ufo_fragment at net/ipv4/udp_offload.c:300 and udp6_ufo_fragment at net/ipv6/udp_offload.c); the outer UDP header bytes at the skb transport offset are packet-supplied attacker-influenced network data on forwarded tunneled traffic. VIOLATED INVARIANT: uh is captured at line 23 as struct udphdr *uh = udp_hdr(skb), a raw pointer into skb->head that must be reloaded after any call that can reallocate the head. pskb_may_pull(skb, tnl_hlen) at line 31 (tnl_hlen = skb_inner_mac_header(skb) - skb_transport_header(skb), line 20, packet-layout dependent) calls __pskb_pull_tail() which, on a cloned or non-linear skb lacking linear tailroom, invokes pskb_expand_head() and frees/replaces skb->head; nothing reloads uh between the pull and its uses. UNSAFE USE: the stale pre-pull uh is dereferenced at line 41 (partial = (__force __wsum)uh->len, SKB_GSO_PARTIAL branch) and line 44 (partial = csum_sub(csum_unfold(uh->check), partial)); 'partial' is the checksum delta later folded into the transmitted UDP header of EVERY generated segment (uh->check = ~csum_fold(csum_add(partial, ...)) at line 131), where uh is only refetched per-segment at line 114 after gso_inner_segment. Same capture -> head-reallocating pull -> stale dereference shape as the seed's pep_get_sb() (ph captured, pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len), ph->sb_type/ph->sb_len through stale ph): a read through possibly-freed slab memory whose value (attacker-relevant checksum/length bytes) is transmitted in packet bytes. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: (1) if the GSO skb is fully linear and uncloned the pull is a no-op and uh stays valid, so triggering requires a cloned/non-linear tunnel GSO skb, which is driver/GRO-path dependent and was not dynamically reproduced; (2) the sibling snapshots s01/s02/s04 reported the identical unpatched shape (facts f008/f015/f018), supporting that this is the persistent unfixed pattern in this corpus rather than a local quirk; (3) the stale reads are read-only and feed only the 'partial' checksum constant, so impact is a KASAN-detectable slab UAF read plus corrupted checksums, not a demonstrated write primitive.

candidates.reason: __skb_udp_tunnel_segment(): uh = udp_hdr(skb) captured at 23; pskb_may_pull(skb, tnl_hlen) at 31 may __pskb_pull_tail -> pskb_expand_head and free skb->head; stale uh->len read at 41 and uh->check read at 44 with no refetch (next refetch only at 114, per-segment after segmentation); stale-derived 'partial' written into every segment's uh->check at 131. Raised as the finding.

udp_gro_receive_segment(): uh = udp_hdr(skb) at 352; the only pulls are skb_gro_pull() at 371 (offset-only bump of NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->data_offset, no head relocation per include/linux/netdevice.h:2658-2661) and skb_gro_postpull_rcsum at 372 (read-only csum adjust); the list-loop reads uh->source at 381 and uh2->len at 392-394 surround skb_gro_receive(p, skb) which appends skb to p/last without freeing p's head, so no captured pointer goes stale. This s05 version has no is_flist/frag-list branch (verified by grep), unlike newer trees.

No stale pointer.

limitations: The finding is a static-analysis hypothesis: no runtime reproducer or KASAN trace was produced in this environment; triggering requires the UDP-tunnel GSO skb to actually be cloned or non-linear at the transport-to-inner-MAC region so pskb_may_pull -> __pskb_pull_tail -> pskb_expand_head really frees the old head (documented semantics in this snapshot's net/core/skbuff.c), which is driver/GRO/forwarding-path dependent and was not dynamically demonstrated on s05.

The skb_gro_header_fast/skb_gro_header_slow census covered every matching call site in net/, include/, and drivers/ of s05 (only vxlan.c and geneve.c in the whole drivers/ tree), but the pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull/linearize inventory was applied to the identified GRO/GSO files (udp/tcp/gre/fou/ip6 offload, af_inet, eth, vlan_core, dev.c core, geneve, vxlan); other GSO segmenters (net/ipv4/esp_offload.c, net/ipv6/esp6_offload.c, net/sctp/offload.c, net/mpls/mpls_gso.c, net/nsh/nsh.c, net/xfrm) were not re-inventoried line-by-line in this pass and could host the same capture->pull->stale-use shape.

Driver-internal ndo_gro_receive wrappers overwhelmingly forward to napi_gro_receive/napi_gro_frags (core audited in net/core/dev.c) and contain no skb_gro_header_slow call sites per the census, but individual driver RX build paths that construct non-linear GRO skbs were not line-by-line audited.

Whether upstream Linux has since fixed __skb_udp_tunnel_segment() could not be checked (no network or Git access); the finding reflects the source as present in snapshots/s05, and the identical unpatched shape independently reported by the parallel s01/s02/s04 gro intents (facts f008/f015/f018) supports but does not prove upstream status.

Frag-list (SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST) and GRO-hint variants of the geneve/udp code that exist in sibling snapshots (s03 fact f017: geneve third skb_gro_header pull with attacker-grown gh_len; udp is_flist branch) do not exist in s05 (verified by grep for is_flist/gro_hint/GRO_HINT), so those specific shapes could not be present here; this absence claim is bounded to those grep patterns.
